accuracy.evidence: Terms checked: learning intention (WALT), success criteria (WILF) and WAGOLL as used in UK primary formative assessment; sharing criteria for success is one of Wiliam's five key strategies (Black and Wiliam); the Year 2 writing quote 'evaluate their writing with the teacher and other pupils' and 're-read to check that their writing makes sense' matches the English programme of study.

misconceptions.evidence: Predictions and feedback target the slips teachers report with success criteria at 6-7: judging by looks (sparkly Card A, glitter, pink, curly letters), saying done without checking (Ben), using the list only at the end (Look first prediction), longer means better, and copying a model word for word.

lab_distinct.evidence: flagcrit is built around a live checklist linked to a card: rows tick or cross from the parts actually on the card, dashed gaps show where a missing part goes, and Ben's card is checked line by line; no other lab models a success-criteria list against a product.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child first finds the four features in the good example, then names them as a list, then uses the list to find Ben's missing words, fixes three cards from the crosses, and finally sees the list tick while building, so the idea look first, check at the end is discovered before the done message states it.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions each have a tempting wrong answer the lab then disproves: the sparkly card is better (it lacks To, words and From), Ben's nice-looking card is done (the list finds no kind words), and look at the list only when finished (the build step shows it guiding the work).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six questions with seven distinct slip messages, for example 'Feeling done is not the same as done. Tick it off with the list to be sure.' and 'Look again: the full stop is there. The first word has no capital letter.'

readability.evidence: Kid text uses short sentences, one idea each, and introduces the phrase success criteria once with its plain meaning; family readability check passes (kid well under 5.0, adult 9.2), and canvas words are one to four words long.

no_filler.evidence: Each kid paragraph does one job (ask first, look at a good one, make the list, check it), the adult notes give terms, sources, four named mistakes and the lab plan, and the family tip is a concrete tick-box routine.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at 360 px and 390 px in both themes: the card and list sit side by side, the tick and cross chips span the width at 56 px buttons, tray tiles show short labels (To, Words, Picture, From, Glitter) without clipping, and every action has a button twin.

accessibility.evidence: Every tap or drag has a labelled button (Add who it is to, On Card B: kind words, It is there, Missing), the canvas aria-label is rewritten after each action, ticks and crosses use symbols as well as colour, and the walkthrough found axe clean in light and dark themes.

sources: Black, P. and Wiliam, D. (1998) Inside the Black Box: Raising Standards Through Classroom Assessment
Clarke, S. (2014) Outstanding Formative Assessment: Culture and Practice
